history.summary: The Jagannath Temple stands on a raised platform several metres above ground in the old part of Alwar city (Nangli Circle/Choti Sabji Mandi area). It is dedicated to Lord Jagannath (Vishnu) in the Puri cult tradition, with SitaramJi and JankiJi in the garbhagriha; unusually, two Jagannath idols reside simultaneously - the older fixed Budhe Jagannath, shown only for five days during Rath Yatra, and a movable utsav murthy. The temple shows medieval-style architecture with rare floral motifs on its walls and gigantic pillars. The annual Rath Yatra carries the movable deity on the Indra Vimana - originally the Maharaja of Alwar's elephant carriage, later donated to the temple - and follows local customs distinct from Puri: it is celebrated as the wedding of Lord Jagannath and JankiJi at Roopbas, with the Tourism Department organising cultural events at the Jagannathji mela. name: Jagannath Temple, Alwar
town_description: Alwar is a historic city in northeastern Rajasthan, about 150 km south of Delhi, once the capital of the Alwar princely state. Its old city is a dense market quarter around the City Palace, Bala Quila and Tripoliya, with the Jagannath Temple standing on a raised platform near Nangli Circle and Choti Sabji Mandi.
